answer: To resist Sybil attacks, implement Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent locks $5,000 in a secure bond. Second, the hardware enclave generates a unique TPM signature. Third, the network verifies this hardware identity. Fourth, any duplicate identity triggers immediate slashing. To reach the zenith of network control, an attacker must endure a cost of $5,000 per node and 72 hours of verification. This ensures they cannot simply harvest the nectar of rewards across a vast digital tundra. It is like a high-walled fortress where every visitor must present a unique, expensive key.
